entries.headline: Ansible docs/slice-testing-strategy.md assumes a push converges nothing; for an Argo CD deploy repo (GitSyncDeploy) a push to main rolls prd
body: slice-testing-strategy.md §4 says 'A push to main no longer converges anything' and §5 says every slice that touches Terraform ends deploy-owed. Both are written for this repo's IaC/* pipelines. A slice targeting an Argo CD deploy repo such as GitSyncDeploy, which this slice does, deploys to prd on the test phase's push and is proven by a live reading inside the run (Ruling D1). The doc says nothing about that kind of slice. The test agent is told to execute this doc, so on such a slice it gets procedure that does not fit.
entries.consequence: On a deploy-repo slice the test agent may treat the push as inert or mark live criteria as owed to the operator, unless the plan's criteria happen to spell the procedure out (043's do).
entries.author: plan-reviewer, planning, r1, plan_review_r1.md

entries.headline: The driver left a scratch clone at /work/scratch/GitSyncDeploy (`Target: github:pvginkel/GitSyncDeploy`)
body: The driver cloned (or adopted) `/work/scratch/GitSyncDeploy` for `Target: github:pvginkel/GitSyncDeploy`; the slice's phases for that repo are branched, merged and pushed there.

Deleting it is safe once the slice's commits are on origin — the push check before the doc phase confirms that. The close-out session removes it then and says so under this entry; nothing is asked of the operator. A clone left in place is synced by every later preflight in this environment and adopted by the next `github:` target naming that repo.
entries.consequence: none — the clone is where the run works; left behind, it takes disk space and a sync in every later preflight, until the close-out session removes it.
entries.author: the driver's target resolution
